findings.problem: The prompt "I don't have [any] money problem" is broken English, since "money problem" needs to be plural or have no article, so the learner gets a garbled sentence to recall from.
"nothing at all" mixes ninguno up with nada (nothing); ninguno means not a single one of something, not nothing.
findings.fix: trick: NINGUNO starts like "nine" and ends with "no": nine? No, not even one.

back.es: ninguno = no, not any, none (negative determiner; ningún before a masculine singular noun, ninguna before a feminine one)
back.example: There isn't any problem. / There's no problem.

note: The card's es is the dictionary form ninguno, but the prompt's slot actually takes ningún, so the hint about shortening is doing real work and should stay.
